title: Soft target update
goal:
Write the target-network update of Section 3, $\theta' \leftarrow \tau\theta + (1-\tau)\theta'$.

- `soft_update(target, source, tau)` takes two dicts that map parameter names to NumPy arrays with the same keys and shapes. It returns a new dict with $\tau\,\text{source} + (1-\tau)\,\text{target}$ for every key. It doesn't modify either input.
- `updates_to_shrink(tau, frac)` returns the smallest integer $n$ such that $(1-\tau)^n \le$ `frac`: the number of updates until the gap between a target and a frozen source falls to a fraction `frac` of its starting size.

The page shows that $\tau = 0.001$ needs 693 updates to halve the gap.
hints: Use a dict comprehension over `target`: `{k: tau * source[k] + (1.0 - tau) * target[k] for k in target}`. The arithmetic creates new arrays, so the inputs stay unchanged.
Take logarithms: $(1-\tau)^n \le f$ means $n \ge \ln f / \ln(1-\tau)$. Both logarithms are negative, so the ratio is positive.
Round up with `math.ceil`. The smallest integer that satisfies the inequality is the ceiling.
